thread:
Leah Kim: Quick sync — running a pressure/warmup + fallback drill for Aperture Dynamics' reserved pool (aperture-resv-09) this Monday 03:00 UTC. Goal: prove queue-shed and graceful degrade behavior under sustained spiky traffic, and verify rollback steps. Runbook: https://playbooks.internal/redwood/aperture-pressure-drill :zap:
Owen Brooks: I can assemble the traffic mix. Thinking steady gen @ 6k rps + chat spikes to 45k rps for 90s, repeated x3 with random jitter. Will tag requests x-test:aperture-1788882000. I'll drop the harness in infra/loaders/aperture-drills.
Diego Morales: I'll watch scaling events, pod churn, allocator logs, and the per-tenant token throttles. If the request queue exceeds 75s median we trigger manual fallback. What fallback policy are we running?
Leah Kim: We'll use 'queue-shed-85pct' for the run — it should start shedding non-critical embed workloads first. Also run KV cold (stop warmers) to exercise cold-starts.
Riley Chen: I'll handle customer comms and billing signalling. I synced with Aperture PM; they asked for a 5m dry-run Sun 22:00 UTC to verify access and certs.
Owen Brooks: Dry-run OK. For the harness I'll use k6 for the gen/embed mix, and vegeta for short chat spike bursts. Example k6 payload:
```js
import http from "k6/http";
import { sleep } from "k6";
export default function() {
  const url = "https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat";
  const payload = JSON.stringify({messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'quick test ' + Math.random()}]});
  http.post(url, payload, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer $TEST", "X-Test-Run": "aperture-1788882000" } });
  sleep(0.02);
}
```
Leah Kim: eng-deploy-bot, run a pre-check for pool health and any required maintenance holds.
eng-deploy-bot: Preflight: pool=aperture-resv-09, gpus=24, headroom=22%, maintenance windows clear, driver versions ok.
Diego Morales: Alerts I'll temporarily set: promql "sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[1m])) by (pool) > 4000" and "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) > 1.5". I'll annotate dashboards and add short-runbook links into the alert.
Leah Kim: Roles & timeline: Sun 22:00 dry-run (10m) -> Mon 03:00 canary burst (3m) -> 03:05 ramp cycles 03:05-03:40 -> 03:40 cool-down + collection. Owen=load, Diego=monitoring/metrics, Riley=customer ops, Leah=orchestration/rollback.
Riley Chen: I've added the customer contact, SRE incident channel, and Zoom link to the calendar event. Also flagged potential renewal talking points if we see >2 degraded outages during the run.
Owen Brooks: Note: I'll disable prefix caching in the harness to ensure more KV miss paths and set a 2% malformed payload rate to exercise error paths.
Diego Morales: Rollback play: 1) pause new routing, 2) re-route traffic to gold fallback model (model-id: rwd-base-1.1), 3) scale-down new pool instances by 30%, 4) lift quota-shed policy after stability. I'll pre-create the k8s drain commands.
Leah Kim: After the run we'll run the quality sampling job (auto) and collect 500 sample outputs per workload for regression. Diego, can you attach the sample collector job to the run?
Diego Morales: Yes — I'll schedule the collector to run at 03:45. Also will export KV hit-rate, gpu_utilization, scale events, and per-verb success_rate to the shared metrics bucket.
Riley Chen: Customer update templated: "We performed a scheduled pressure test to validate autoscale and fallback behavior; expected to see degraded latency under peak; no customer-facing outage planned." I'll post the postmortem note and link to the samples once ready.
Leah Kim: Final pre-checks: 1) disable warmers, 2) push temp-alert thresholds, 3) set quota policy=queue-shed-85pct, 4) load harness branch merged by EOW. We'll reconfirm here 2h before windows. Thanks all — see you in the incident channel. :white_check_mark:
